title: Add compact 'sparkline' RAG playbook + offline assertion runner quickstart
author: Ava Moreno
description: Context: Teams often need minimal, offline-capable RAG playbooks for rapid iteration and reproducible assertions. This PR introduces a compact 'sparkline' RAG quickstart that focuses on small indexed corpora, deterministic tool-calling examples, and an offline assertion runner for CI-free validation. Motivation: provide a tiny, copy-pasteable example that engineers can use in local dev loops, CI smoke tests, and sandboxed workshops without requiring a full vector DB or remote telemetry. What this PR delivers: 1) a new quickstart at quickstarts/sparkline-playbook with a README that includes step-by-step local setup (seeded index, minimal retriever, and tool stubs); 2) an offline assertion runner (playback/assert-runner.py) that replays an input sequence and validates structured outputs against JSON schemas and fuzzy-similarity thresholds; 3) a curated 50-document sample corpus in newline-delimited JSON format to keep indexing and runtime cheap; 4) compact examples of tool-calling patterns (weather lookup and calendar stubs) with deterministic, test-friendly stubs; 5) a docs.site nav entry and shortguide snippet to appear on the quickstarts index; 6) a lightweight telemetry sparklines reporter that surfaces per-step latency and token counts in the runner output (no external metrics backend). Migration notes: no breaking changes to public APIs. The quickstart uses the same SDK entrypoints as existing examples but pins versions in the README for deterministic boots. Checklist: • Add playbook skeleton and sample corpus ✓ • Implement assertion runner and schema checks ✓ • Add deterministic tool stubs and example traces ✓ • Add docs.site nav entry and quickstarts index blurb ✓ • Add CI smoke test for the runner and fix flakiness from initial run ✓ Usage summary: clone repo, cd quickstarts/sparkline-playbook, python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt, ./scripts/build_index.sh --source sample-corpus.jsonl, python playbook_runner.py --profile local --assertions assertions.jsonl. The README includes a minimal prompt template and tips for converting to Hosted/Dedicated flows. CI notes: initial run failed due to an asynchronous file handle in the indexer; fixed in commit 3 by switching to context-managed I/O and adding a small sleep in the smoke harness. Tests: added unit tests for the assertion runner and an integration smoke test that runs in ~18s on GitHub Actions. Review summary: reviewers requested clearer error messages for failed assertions and a shorter default corpus; both were addressed. Merge: squash and merge after approvals. Related: pairs well with ENG-1872 (mini-authoring kit) and PM-402 (quickstarts prioritization).

release_notes: Introduce a compact RAG 'sparkline' quickstart with an offline assertion runner and deterministic tool stubs. Useful for local dev loops, smoke CI, and workshops. No breaking API changes.
